links.comparator_used: Usual care without a referral notification: patients in the control arm were also flagged by the algorithm and reviewed by palliative specialists, but their PCPs were not messaged, so they could still be referred through usual pathways.
links.outcome: Time to 0.1% of the primary care population receiving a palliative care consultation (primary outcome); time to consultation being ordered. Secondary outcomes were time to advance care planning note and time to palliative care ICD-10 code.
links.effect: Consultation completed: 60.9 (47.8–79.4) vs 71.8 (50.9–103.8) days, posterior probability of a shorter time with intervention 0.88. Consultation ordered: 42.8 (34.5–54.2) vs 63.9 (46.8–90.1) days, probability >0.99. Advance care planning note: median effect 1.04 (0.81–1.35), probability 0.64. Palliative care ICD-10 code: 1.03 (0.87–1.24), probability 0.64.
links.tradeoff: Algorithm PPV was only 0.18 (273/1512 presentations accepted by specialists). Each case needed specialist chart review, adding burden in busy primary care practices. Only 50.7% of notified patients had a consultation ordered and 26.1% completed one. Barriers such as patient disinterest and scheduling limited the effect on completed consultations.
links.quote: For the primary outcome of time to a palliative care consultation, the median (95% credible interval) time to 0.1% of the primary care adult population receiving the consultation was 60.9 (47.8–79.4) days for the intervention, as compared with 71.8 (50.9–103.8) days for the control (posterior probability of a shorter time with the intervention, 0.88; Fig. 2 ).

design_hint: specialist review of algorithm flags before PCP referral notification
